sentences.text:
Shiv Kumar Vaishya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25
March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:24531
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Hon'Ble Shri Justice Deepak Khot
 On The 25th Of March, 2026
 Writ Petition No. 12975 of 2013
 Shiv Kumar Vaishya
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri B.K. Bais - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri V.S. Chourdhary - Government Adv
 respondent/State.

Shri Himanshu Shukla - Advocate for respondent No.4.
 Order

The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking following reliefs :
"1. Direct the respondents to pay the compensation as per current market rate or allot the land in lieu of the land.
2. Any other relief or writ or direction or order which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper looking to the facts and circumstances of the case be kindly awarded to the petitioner including the cost of the petition."

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the land owner of the land bearing Khasra No.1236/2 Kha admeasuring area 0.83 Hectare situated at village Siddhi Kala,
Tehsil and District NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24531 2 WP-12975-2013 Singrauli.
It is further submitted that without compensation and without adopting due procedure of law, land excess to the notification of acquisition has been taken over by the respondents.

It is submitted that this Court vide order dated 29.07.2013 has granted interim relief in favour of the petitioner restraining the respondents from taking possession in excess to the area mentioned in the notification Annexure P/2 under Section 9(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that despite of the order, the possession has been taken over,
however, this controversy cannot be resolved by this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India as disputed question of facts are involved.

sentences.text: The counsel for the petitioner has graciously submitted that the dispute in regard to boundary and possession of excess land can be resolved by demarcation by the respondent/State authority for which the correction in the map has already been done and his application for demarcation is pending.
However, as the said application is not on record, therefore, no direction on the said prayer can be made.

Accordingly, the petition is disposed of with the direction that in case the petitioner files an appropriate application under Section 129 of MPLRC for demarcation of his land on the basis of the existing map, within 15 days from today alongwith certified copy of this order, the authority shall decide the said application within two months from the date of receipt of application and certified copy of this order.

If in the demarcation, it is found that the land in excess to the notification has been taken over by the respondents, then petitioner shall be at liberty to file appropriate application before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24531 3 WP-12975-2013 appropriate forum for adequate compensation, in accordance with law.
It is expected from the authority that the same shall be decided in accordance with law.
With the aforesaid, the petition is disposed of.

(DEEPAK KHOT) JUDGE anand Shiv Kumar Vaishya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41689182/
